Bill Orcutt :: Four Louies Live Posted on September 3, 2026 September 2, 2026 Orcutt’s deconstruction of “Louie Louie” is a mash-up of Steve Reich’s 1970 minimalist milestones “Four Organs” with the rock staple. It finds a seam between experimental, avant garde repetition and the dumb but beautiful way that garage rock can hammer on a riff forever. The piece first emerged as a studio album on Fake Estates in 2024. This live recording revisits the piece in all its organ-stabbing, maraca-shaking glory. American Spring :: S/T (1972) Posted on September 2, 2026 September 1, 2026 Constantly meandering in copyright turmoil that renders it inaccessible, 1972’s lone eponymous record by American Spring (sisters Marilyn Wilson and Diane Rovell, formerly of girl group The Honeys) is an obtusely captivating slice of baroque pop. A production of Marilyn’s husband Brian Wilson along with consummate Beach Boys engineer Stephen Desper, the source material culls tracks from the band’s classic Sunflower as well as the The Shirelles, old country standards and the Goffin-King and Tommy Roe songbooks. Brazilians love covering the Fab Four in all the different styles (from bossa to Tropícalia and MPB), but some intrepid brasileiros prefer to explore other international trends. Melô do Embaixador digs deep into the country’s under-documented history of American soul, funk, and disco, turning up 27 strange and compelling interpretations from 1968 to 2015. Tim Maia, forgotten bandleaders, anonymous studio bands, disco cash-ins, and one-hit wonders all make appearances, some translated into Portuguese, some in instrumental versions, some in endearingly awkward English, and all revealing a parallel history of Brazilian popular music that has largely escaped critical attention. The results range from faithful to bizarre, but they all make a compelling case for hearing these records on their own terms.
